w10_T4_009952: A runner trained for a race that would take 3 hours. He started with 87 calories to burn. He divided his workout into thirds, burning 29 calories in each third. He then burned 5 times that amount during the main race. Unfortunately, 102 calories were lost due to measurement error. His final burn total decreased by 17 more. How many calories did he burn in total?
w10_T4_009953: Lisa had 218 dollars in her checking account. In the morning, she deposited 6 dollars. At noon, she added 9 dollars more. By afternoon, she added 16 dollars. At that point, 204 dollars were withdrawn for bills. By evening, 25 dollars were removed for groceries. Her brother Mike had 150 dollars (kept in a separate account). What was Lisa's final account balance in dollars?
w10_T4_009956: An estate sale started with 189 items for auction. In the morning, 147 items were sold. By afternoon, the remaining items were marked at 5 times their original value. Then 136 dollars in fees were deducted. By evening, 52 dollars were added as a bonus. How much total value remained after all changes?
w10_T4_009958: A garden started with 23 tomato plants. In the morning, 19 more were planted. By afternoon, 22 additional plants were added. Each plant would grow 5 tomatoes. Then 41 more tomatoes were harvested from other vines. How many tomatoes would be produced in total?
w10_T4_009959: A production line started with 52 items per hour in the morning. By mid-morning, the rate multiplied by 7 (faster machines). By afternoon, it doubled to 7 times the doubled amount. Then 5 bonus items were added per hour. By evening, the hourly rate multiplied by 6. What was the final hourly production rate?
w10_T4_009961: A factory had 166 workers. In the morning shift, the workforce multiplied by 6. At lunch, the crew was split equally in half. In the afternoon, they split again in thirds. By the evening, the group multiplied by 8. Finally, 423 workers left for the day. How many workers remained?
w10_T4_009963: A student started with 226 homework problems to complete. In the morning, they completed 14 problems. By mid-day, they had 6 times as many left (from the remaining). Then they received 45 additional problems. By evening, they had completed 209 problems total. How many problems still remained?
w10_T4_009964: A restaurant served 223 customers at opening. By morning rush, 30 more arrived. The customer count then multiplied by 9 for peak lunch. By afternoon, 19 additional customers were seated. Evening brought 27 more. Finally, the count doubled for the night shift projection. After all this, how many customers did the restaurant project for the night?
w10_T4_009974: A concert promoter sold 44 tickets in the morning. By noon, they multiplied by 9. Then they added 23 more tickets. The total tripled by afternoon. By evening, 23 additional tickets were added. Finally, the count multiplied by 9 for the estimate. How many tickets did they estimate to sell?
w10_T4_009986: A workshop had 91 participants in the morning. By afternoon, 12 left early. Then 23 joined from another session. The group multiplied by 5 for a group project. By evening, the number doubled. The final count was divided into 5 equal learning groups. How many people were in each group?
w10_T4_009994: A project had 24 tasks initially. In the morning, 43 tasks were added. By noon, 2 tasks were completed and removed. By afternoon, 50 tasks were combined into other projects. The remaining tasks tripled for tracking purposes. Throughout the day, a related project had 80 tasks (not included here). How many tasks remained for this project?
w10_T4_009999: Sarah had 84 dollars to spend. She added 69 dollars from her paycheck. The total multiplied by 5 for her investment goal. Then she added 65 more dollars. She added another 37 dollars from a bonus. A distractor: her friend had 95 dollars (not part of this calculation). How much did Sarah end up with?
w10_T4_010006: A warehouse had 183 boxes in the morning. By mid-morning, 165 boxes were shipped out. At lunch, 14 more were removed. By afternoon, 1 final box was taken. The remaining boxes were tripled for inventory multiplication. His colleague had 120 boxes in a different location. How many boxes were in the final inventory?
w10_T4_010007: A store started with 160 items. In the morning, the count multiplied by 8. By afternoon, the inventory was split into 5 equal departments. Then 103 items were sold. By evening, 71 items arrived. What was the final inventory count?
w10_T4_010008: A production started with 149 units in the morning. By mid-morning, 113 were rejected. The remaining units multiplied by 8. By lunch, the batch was divided in half. Then 51 units were lost in transport. In the afternoon, the count multiplied by 7. By evening, everything multiplied by 6. How many units were produced by day end?
w10_T4_010009: An account had 203 dollars. By morning, 111 dollars were spent. The remaining amount was divided equally into 4 parts. Then 4 dollars were deducted from the total. By afternoon, 36 dollars were added. By evening, 13 dollars were withdrawn. Meanwhile, a related account had 50 dollars. How much was left in the account?
w10_T4_010012: A project started with 89 hours of work. By morning, 34 hours were completed. The remaining hours multiplied by 8 for estimation. Then 218 hours were already accounted for. An additional 58 hours were subtracted. Finally, 20 more hours were removed as unnecessary. How many hours remained?
w10_T4_010017: A fund had 184 dollars initially. By morning, 77 dollars were withdrawn. By midday, 64 dollars were deposited. By afternoon, 54 dollars arrived. Then 172 dollars were removed for expenses. Finally, 73 dollars were added back. A distractor: another fund had 95 dollars elsewhere. What was the fund balance?
w10_T4_010021: A class started with 102 students. In the morning, the enrollment multiplied by 6. By midday, this doubled by 5. By afternoon, another multiplication by 3. Then 70 more students were added for the evening session. His adjacent class had 95 students (separate). How many total did the class grow to?
w10_T4_010025: A project budget started at 231 dollars. In the morning phase, 61 dollars were added. By midday, the budget multiplied by 6. By afternoon, it multiplied by 3 more. By evening, 4329 dollars were spent. How much remained in the budget?
w10_T4_010044: A gym had 110 members initially. In the morning, membership multiplied by 5. By afternoon, 70 more joined. The total was then split into 4 training groups. By evening, 70 members left. How many remained in the gym?
w10_T4_010057: A supply chain had 123 items at opening. In the morning, the count multiplied by 7. By midday, 28 items were used. The inventory multiplied by 7 for the afternoon count. By evening, 48 more items arrived. Finally, 3762 items were shipped out for distribution. How many items remained in stock?
w10_T4_010060: A worker had 35 tasks to complete. In the morning, they started with 1 task left to assign. By mid-morning, the workload multiplied by 7. By noon, 14 tasks were completed. By afternoon, the remaining multiplied by 9. By evening, another multiplication by 5 occurred. His co-worker had similar tasks. How many tasks did the worker track?
w10_T4_010066: A budget started at 85 dollars. In the morning, 66 dollars were added. By noon, 35 more were contributed. By afternoon, 16 dollars were removed. Then 168 dollars were spent on supplies. The final remaining amount multiplied by 9. Throughout this process, the total was measured in hours (a unit conversion). How much was the final budget?
w10_T4_010078: A product started with 97 units. In the morning, production multiplied by 8. By afternoon, output multiplied by 4 more. Then 53 units were added from a shipment. By evening, 3030 units were removed for distribution. The count was measured in bundles of items. How many units remained in storage?
